tasks.spec:
You are an implementation worker writing a NEW certification checker. Write exactly ONE file in your current working directory: ./resolution_check.py. READ access to /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast; never write to it. Pure stdlib + numpy + ffmpeg/ffprobe subprocess. No git, no MCP, no network.

WHY THIS GATE EXISTS (a real, shipped defect). A podcast pipeline recorded a host at 1920x1080 and a guest at 1280x720, then hard-coded every intermediate speaker stem to 960x540 and finally UPSCALED back to a 1920x1080 master. The master's container therefore ADVERTISED 1080p while carrying only 540p of real picture: measured high-frequency detail was 2.1 versus 3.0 for the same subject in the raw camera file. Eight certification gates passed it. A container-dimension check alone would ALSO have passed it — so this gate must measure REAL detail, not just width and height.

FILE CONTRACT: ./resolution_check.py with argparse:
  resolution_check.py --final PATH --sources PATH [PATH ...] [--min-detail-ratio 0.75] [--probe-count 5] [--json OUT]
  resolution_check.py --self-test
Exit 0 when every check passes, 1 on any FAIL, 2 on unusable inputs.

CHECKS:
1. DECLARED_RESOLUTION: ffprobe the final's width/height. Report them. FAIL if either dimension is smaller than the LARGEST source camera's corresponding dimension (delivering below what was captured is silent quality loss). Sources smaller than the final are fine (a 720p guest on a 1080p canvas).
2. REAL_DETAIL: the core of the gate. For --probe-count evenly spaced timestamps in the final's middle 80% (avoid bumpers at head/tail), decode one frame from the final and one frame from the source that best matches it, scale BOTH to a common comparison size (the smaller of the two native heights, so neither is unfairly upscaled), convert to gray, and compute a detail score = mean absolute value of the horizontal+vertical first-difference (a cheap sharpness proxy). Report the final's median detail, the source's median detail, and the ratio. FAIL when ratio < --min-detail-ratio. Because encoder and content differences add noise, use the MEDIAN across probes, not a single frame.
   Source-frame matching: you cannot assume time alignment between the final (edited, bumper-prefixed) and a raw source. So do NOT try to match timestamps. Instead compute each file's OWN median detail over its own probe set (same probe count, middle 80%, same comparison size) and compare those distributions. State this explicitly in the output so a reader knows it is a distribution comparison, not a frame-pair comparison.
3. UPSCALE_FINGERPRINT: an independent, timestamp-free signal for upscaling. Downscale the final's frame by 2 and re-upscale it by 2, then measure how little the detail changes: a genuinely sharp 1080p frame LOSES significant detail through that round trip, while a frame that was already upscaled from 540p barely changes. Report the retention ratio (detail after round-trip / detail before) and FAIL when retention exceeds UPSCALE_RETENTION_MAX (named constant, 0.92) which indicates the image carries no true detail at its claimed resolution. Explain the number in the WHY line.

SELF-TEST (--self-test, hermetic, ffmpeg lavfi only, no repo access): synthesize a detailed 1920x1080 source (e.g. a high-frequency test pattern plus noise: testsrc2 or a noise-filled frame — must contain real fine detail). Then build (a) a GOOD final: the source encoded at 1920x1080 directly; (b) a BAD final: the source downscaled to 960x540 and re-upscaled to 1920x1080 (exactly the shipped defect). Assert, printing every measured number: the GOOD final passes all three checks and exits 0; the BAD final FAILS REAL_DETAIL or UPSCALE_FINGERPRINT and exits 1; and a final whose declared height is BELOW the source height FAILS DECLARED_RESOLUTION. Self-test exits 0 only when green cases are green and red cases red. Tune the constants so the synthetic BAD case is caught with margin, and print the margin.

Every threshold a named constant with a one-line rationale. No hard-coded episode paths.

tasks.verified: master proven to carry real detail at its declared resolution; catches the 540p-upscaled-to-1080p defect

tasks.spec:
You are an implementation worker writing a NEW certification checker. Write exactly ONE file in your current working directory: ./clip_framing_check.py. READ access to /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast; never write to it. Pure stdlib + numpy + OpenCV (cv2) + ffmpeg subprocess. No git, no MCP, no network.

WHY THIS GATE EXISTS (a real, shipped defect). A vertical 9:16 promo clip was generated by cropping the "guest half" of the program frame, on the assumption the program is a side-by-side two-camera layout. The program is actually angle-switched: one speaker fills the whole frame. The shipped clip therefore showed the WALL BEHIND the guest for its entire duration — no face anywhere — while the same moment in the program showed the speaker centered. Existing gates verified the clip's AUDIO matched its claimed source and passed it. Nothing looked at the picture. This gate looks at the picture.

FILE CONTRACT: ./clip_framing_check.py with argparse:
  clip_framing_check.py --clips-dir PATH [--manifest PATH] [--min-face-coverage 0.5] [--max-center-offset 0.28] [--min-face-height 0.10] [--samples 9] [--json OUT]
  clip_framing_check.py --self-test
Exit 0 when every clip passes, 1 on any FAIL, 2 on unusable inputs (no clips found, cv2 missing, unreadable video). Note: cv2 missing must be exit 2 UNMEASURABLE, never a silent pass.

PER CLIP (every video file in --clips-dir, or those named in --manifest):
1. FACE_COVERAGE: sample --samples evenly spaced frames; run OpenCV haarcascade_frontalface_default (cv2.data.haarcascades) on each, taking the largest detection per frame. coverage = fraction of sampled frames containing a face. FAIL when coverage < --min-face-coverage. WHY line must say a promo clip with no face in most frames is framed on the wrong subject.
2. FACE_CENTERING: for frames with a face, compute the face center's horizontal position as a fraction of frame width; take the median; offset = |median - 0.5|. FAIL when offset > --max-center-offset (the subject is jammed against an edge). Report the median position and the offset.
3. FACE_SIZE: median face height as a fraction of frame height. FAIL when below --min-face-height — a face present but tiny means the crop framed the room, not the person.
4. ASPECT: report each clip's dimensions and flag when a clip named/declared vertical is not portrait (height > width), and vice versa for landscape. This is a FAIL, since a mis-shaped clip is unusable on its target platform.
Print one line per clip per check with the measured numbers, and a final summary line. Robustness: a clip that cannot be decoded is exit 2, not skipped silently.

SELF-TEST (--self-test, hermetic, no repo access): you cannot rely on a real face image, so GENERATE one procedurally that the Haar cascade actually detects, then VERIFY the cascade detects it before using it as the green fixture — if your synthetic face is not detected, iterate the drawing (ellipse head, darker eye regions, mouth line, appropriate contrast and size) until detection succeeds; a self-test whose green case is undetectable is a broken self-test, so print the detection result for the fixture. Build with ffmpeg/OpenCV: (a) GOOD clip: 1080x1920 portrait, synthetic face centered, occupying a realistic fraction of the height; (b) BAD-no-face clip: the same size showing only a textured wall (no face) — must FAIL FACE_COVERAGE; (c) BAD-edge clip: the face pushed to the far left edge — must FAIL FACE_CENTERING; (d) BAD-aspect clip: landscape dimensions while declared vertical — must FAIL ASPECT. Assert every case, printing measured numbers, and exit 0 only when green is green and all three reds are red.

Every threshold a named constant with a one-line rationale. No hard-coded episode paths or names.
